canonical_statement: Provisional source-faithful root: for a triangular array of row-wise independent, centered, square-integrable real random variables, if each row's total variance is one and the Lindeberg truncated-second-moment condition holds for every positive epsilon, then the sum of each row converges in distribution to the standard normal law.
domain_and_universes: Planned: a measurable probability space and a Nat-indexed triangular array of real-valued random variables; exact universes and finite-row index type remain open
quantifiers: triangular array X(n,k) of real random variables
each row index n and its finite column range
hypotheses: the sum of variances in every row is one
Lindeberg sums tend to zero for every positive epsilon
conclusion: The row sums converge in distribution to the standard Gaussian distribution

alternate_encodings.target: unnormalized variance s_n^2 with row sum divided by s_n
Lindeberg iff Gaussian convergence under the Feller/uniform-negligibility condition
alternate_encodings.relationship: stronger converse formulation often called Lindeberg-Feller

excluded_degenerate_cases: Zero total row variance is excluded by unit normalization; epsilon is strictly positive; empty-row and zero-variance encodings require explicit statement-phase boundary tests.
